plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Per-project IaaS quotas exist (vcpu, ram in MiB, volumes, gigabytes, publicIps, snapshots, backups, networks, nics, securityGroups) via GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/regions/{region}/quotas; default values for new projects are not published.

free.note: No public free tier or trial credit. Startup Program gives negotiated credits (EU-HQ startups only).

caveats: OS disks, IP, snapshots, stopped state and egress not flattened from full PIM dataset.

Unknowns remain null, not free. Single-AZ and Metro HA servers are ordinary self-serve GA VMs (PIM API maturityModelState "ga", re-checked 2026-09-28), so they carry no alt flag; Metro HA is the same flavour at 2x price with metro redundancy. CPU overcommit differs by family: "d"-suffix flavours (c1a/c2a/g1a/g2a/m1a/m2a/b*a/g1r) have dedicated vCPUs; c1/c2i/g1/g2i/m1/m2i/s1/t1/t2i are cpuOverprovisioning:true (shared, no published baseline). *3i families are cpuOverprovisioning:false in PIM but listed under CPU-overprovisioning Intel Gen3 in the docs (conflict).
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Official price-list preamble: net list prices plus applicable taxes and duties.
Residency: eu01 Germany and eu02 Austria; captured example eu01. Country control is not certification of all dependent services.

Hourly billing per started hour: 'The services will be invoiced to the originating cost centers per billing unit or part thereof' and server billing unit is 'per hour'. Per-month price-list figures are 720-h projections, not caps.

Region eu02 (Austria): server flavours cost the same as eu01, but only *2a/*3i families are offered (no c1/c2i/c1a, so the cheapest 4/8 there is c3i.4 USD 0.1978/h); block storage, snapshots and IPv4 are about 5% dearer in eu02.
Size pricing is not linear within a family: c2i.2 (2/4) EUR 0.0433/h but c2i.4 (4/8) EUR 0.1533/h (3.5x). Two c2i.2 VMs cost less than one c2i.4.
Beta flavours u2i.38d/76d/152d (up to 152 vCPU / 5700 GB, EUR 12.9-48.3/h) are in PIM with maturityModelState 'beta' and priceListVisibility 'No'.
The first Virtual Network in each project automatically gets a bound public IP (~$3.37/month, the ipv4_month rate), billed even if the VMs use no public IP.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Stopping the STACKIT Server won't remove the allocation and keep all its resources reserved for faster startup. Deallocating corresponds to stopping the STACKIT Server and removing its allocation... Deallocating doesn't delete the STACKIT Server or its resources.
snapshot_auto.note: Stop/deallocate just leaves the persistent volume attached (or reserved) - there is no automatic memory/disk snapshot taken on stop/timeout and restored on start. Snapshots exist only as a separate, explicitly-triggered feature (on-demand or scheduled backups via Server Backup Management), never tied to the stop action itself. Confirms the card's 'no'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: To restore a volume you first need to create a new volume and provide the source-type of “snapshot” or “backup” with the corresponding id.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Volume snapshots and volume backups via IaaS API (POST /snapshots 'Create a new Snapshot from a Volume in a project', POST /backups) and Portal; disk only, no memory. New servers boot from a volume created from a snapshot/backup or from a cloned volume (documented 'clone a VM' flow: --boot-volume-source-type volume); volumes can also be turned into images.

harness_api.quote: With the Server Agent, you can run custom Shell and PowerShell scripts directly on your STACKIT servers. This lets you perform individual tasks, automate workflows, or handle bulk operations without manual intervention.
harness_api.note: STACKIT Compute Engine is plain IaaS (KVM/OpenStack VMs). Its only exec-style API is the Server Agent, a generic remote shell/PowerShell script runner (an exec API) - there is no API to prompt/stream/follow-up with a coding agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) running inside the VM. Outside the scope of a bare VM product; confirms the card's 'no'.

egress_allowlist.quote: Egress rules control outgoing traffic from your servers. By default there is a rule that allows all egress traffic. You can create restrictive egress rules to:
egress_allowlist.note: Stateful Security Groups on the NIC (NIC Security enabled by default): allow-only rules by direction, protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP/any), port range and IP/CIDR or remote security group; remove the default allow-all egress rule to get default-deny. Free. No domain-level filtering. Servers can also run without public IP.

ingress_rules.quote: Ingress (Inbound): All incoming traffic is blocked by default, with one important exception—traffic from instances within the same Security Group is allowed
ingress_rules.note: Inbound allow rules by protocol/port/source CIDR or security group; public IPs are optional per NIC.

guest_firewall.quote: Use a firewall, for example with iptables or firewalld, and allow only necessary ports.

secret_proxy.quote: Store secrets like passwords, configuration files and text separated from your code ... Automation and integrations via API
secret_proxy.note: STACKIT Secrets Manager is a Vault-based secret store that applications/workloads read from (via API/AppRole) - the secret still reaches the caller/VM, it is not a first-party HTTP-injecting proxy that keeps credentials out of the machine. On a plain IaaS VM product, secrets otherwise arrive as cloud-init user data or attached service accounts (env/files). Confirms the card's 'no'.

volume_attach.quote: This tutorial will guide you through the process of creating additional storage volumes on the STACKIT portal.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage volumes, same availability zone only ('only servers in the same AZ can use the volume'); attach via Portal or API (servers/{id}/volume-attachments); single-attach (Volume has one serverId); resizable; performance classes.

volume_shared.quote: A Share Export Policy is a set of rules that control client access to the data storied in the NFS Shares. This is where you can define which IPs can mount the NFS Shares and which type of access these IPs have.
volume_shared.note: STACKIT File Storage (SFS): NFS Resource Pools (500 GB-20 TB, mountable read-only) containing NFS Shares mountable read-write by any client IPs allowed by the Share Export Policy ('NFS Shares can be mounted in read and write mode'); requires a STACKIT Network Area with routing tables. Separate paid product. Block volumes themselves are single-attach.

isolation.quote: If you have an image in a format that is not accepted by STACKIT, you can convert it to the raw format using QEMU.
isolation.note: derived: STACKIT Compute Engine is an OpenStack-style IaaS (server/volume/network-area API) that accepts raw/qcow2/iso QEMU disk images for custom VMs; this is standard for OpenStack Nova compute running libvirt+KVM. Hypervisor is never explicitly named 'KVM' in public STACKIT docs.

image_oci.quote: should be replaced with the format of your image (possible formats: “raw”,“qcow2”,“iso”)
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Custom images are VM disk images (raw/qcow2/iso), not Docker/OCI container images; Compute Engine is an IaaS VM product, not a container runtime.

docker_inside.quote: Use a firewall, for example with iptables or firewalld, and allow only necessary ports.
docker_inside.note: derived: full KVM/OpenStack-style VM with root access (root: true); Docker/containers run inside like on any Linux VM. Not explicitly documented by STACKIT as a supported use case.

desktop.quote: The web console is an emulated console access to the VM. For this reason, the copy/paste function, for example, is not available.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The Portal 'web console' is an emergency emulated text/serial console for troubleshooting, not a graphical desktop (VNC/RDP/stream).

browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Plain IaaS VM/server product; no managed browser is provided or documented.

computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot/click-driving API exists for an IaaS VM product.

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. STACKIT sells VMs/infrastructure, not a browser-automation/stealth product.

captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Plain IaaS VM; no CAPTCHA-solving service documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: Technically this is done by source NAT (SNAT) in combination with masquerading. When creating the first network in a public project, STACKIT automatically creates and assigns a public IP for all Virtual Networks.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic uses STACKIT-owned datacenter IP ranges (SNAT gateway IP or an attached STACKIT Public IP Address), not residential/mobile IPs.

fork.quote: Create a new volume which uses the old volume as its source, this creates a clone. ... Create a new VM using the cloned drive
fork.note: Documented clone workflow: clone the boot volume of an existing server, then create a new server booting from the cloned volume.

fork_running.quote:
STATE	ACTIVE
POWER STATUS	RUNNING ... stackit volume create --availability-zone eu01-1 --source-type volume --source-id b4c68c72-6130-443e-8cb2-d5db753280d6 --name clone-volume
fork_running.note: The documented clone tutorial clones the boot volume of a server shown as STATE ACTIVE / POWER STATUS RUNNING without any step to stop the source VM first.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Clone the Boot Volume ... Create a new VM using the cloned drive
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Cloning only duplicates the boot volume (disk); the new VM boots fresh from that disk. No memory/process state is captured or restored.

wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Plain always-on/stoppable IaaS VMs; no request-triggered auto-wake mechanism is documented.

auto_stop_idle.note: No idle-detection auto-stop/auto-sleep feature documented for Compute Engine servers; VMs run until explicitly stopped (pause_resume is manual).

live_resize.quote: By changing the machine-type the server will have a short downtime.
live_resize.note: Changing CPU/RAM (machine-type) requires the documented resize operation, which causes a short downtime -- not a live/hot resize.

agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Server Agent/Run Command only executes arbitrary shell/PowerShell scripts; no coding-agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) templates or preinstalls are offered.

own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. STACKIT has no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: total_count: 0 (search for an 'mcp' named repo under the stackitcloud GitHub org)
mcp_server.note: No MCP server repository found under the stackitcloud GitHub org; none documented on docs.stackit.cloud either.

lang_python.quote: The STACKIT Linux Server is built on the STACKIT Compute Engine and provides virtual machines (VMs) for running Linux-based operating systems.
lang_python.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Bare OS VM images (RHEL/Ubuntu/Windows/etc.); no managed Python runtime layer -- the customer installs whatever language runtimes they need.

lang_node.quote: The STACKIT Linux Server is built on the STACKIT Compute Engine and provides virtual machines (VMs) for running Linux-based operating systems.
lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Bare OS VM images; no managed Node.js runtime is preinstalled or offered -- the customer installs it themselves.

inbound_https.quote: It supports outbound internet access but does not allow traffic initiated from the public internet to reach your resources.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Reaching a VM requires attaching a raw STACKIT Public IP Address and opening security-group ports yourself; there is no managed HTTPS-URL-to-port feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: Egress rules control outgoing traffic from your servers. By default there is a rule that allows all egress traffic.
egress_http_rules.note: Security Group egress rules operate at protocol/port/IP-CIDR level only (already recorded as egress_allowlist level: 'ip'); there is no HTTP method/path-level egress control.

static_egress_ip.quote: When creating the first network in a public project, STACKIT automatically creates and assigns a public IP for all Virtual Networks.
static_egress_ip.note: Each Virtual Network gets a fixed bound public (SNAT) IP for outbound traffic, and a dedicated STACKIT Public IP Address can also be attached per VM/NIC; both are static/persistent, not rotating.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Compute Engine offers Linux and Windows server VMs on standard x86/ARM cloud hardware; no macOS/Apple-silicon VMs are offered.

self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. STACKIT is a hyperscaler cloud service run in STACKIT's own datacenters; it is not distributed as software you run on your own infrastructure.

byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Compute Engine runs exclusively in STACKIT's own EU datacenters (eu01/eu02); it is not deployed into a customer's own cloud account.

open_source.note: STACKIT Compute Engine is a proprietary managed cloud service operated by Schwarz Digits/STACKIT; the product itself (control plane, portal, billing) is not released under an OSI license, even though it is OpenStack-influenced under the hood.

hipaa.quote: STACKIT - The sovereign cloud for companies
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. STACKIT is an EU/German-Austrian sovereign cloud (GDPR/regional focus); no BAA or HIPAA-eligibility program is documented for a US healthcare regulation.

sso.quote: Set up SAML federation with STACKIT IdP by following these steps. The STACKIT IdP acts as the Service Provider (SP), and your organization’s system acts as the Identity Provider (IdP).
sso.note: STACKIT IdP supports both SAML 2.0 federation and Generic OIDC 1.0 federation for customer organizations.

max_session_h.quote: The services will be invoiced to the originating cost centers per billing unit or part thereof
max_session_h.note: Compute Engine servers are billed hourly and run indefinitely until the customer stops/deletes them; there is no maximum session duration enforced by STACKIT.

usage_api.quote: The cost API provides detailed reports on the costs for a customer or project over a certain amount of time. GetCostsForProject and ListCostsForCustomer endpoints return ProjectCostWithDetailedServices containing per-service breakdown with TotalCharge and TotalDiscount values in cents
usage_api.note: granularity: per-project; cost: yes; API accessible via STACKIT SDKs (Go, Python, Java) and REST. Supports project-level cost queries with optional service-level detail via granularity parameter. ReportData provides time-period breakdowns.
